entry.title: The Rhetoric Practitioner
entry.summary: A working communicator mining Aristotle's Rhetoric for persuasion technique, wanting cross-referenced, footnoted primary text.
entry.content:
This reader already knows why persuasion matters; they come to Aristotle’s Rhetoric looking for technique they can put to work, not a survey of classical philosophy. They might be preparing a speech, coaching a debate team, or writing professionally, and they treat the text as a working reference rather than a cover-to-cover read.

What they need most is a primary text they can navigate non-linearly: reliable cross-references between related passages, footnotes that connect a classical example to its modern analogue, and enough structural clarity to jump straight to the chapter that covers the technique they are after. They are less concerned with the text’s historical context than with whether a given passage still holds up as usable guidance.

They measure a converted showcase page as successful when they can find the passage that names a specific persuasive technique, understand it well enough to apply it, and trace it back to the original wording if they need to cite or quote it.
